NVDA.text: Nvidia fell 1.0% as semiconductor weakness persisted despite Treasury-driven relief in long-term yields; no fresh Nvidia-specific catalyst was confirmed.

AVGO.text: Broadcom fell 4.6% after Marvell unveiled an expanded custom-AI-chip deal with Google, raising concerns that Google is diversifying spending beyond Broadcom even though analysts cautioned the new programs may not directly displace its core TPU work.

TSM.text: TSM slipped 0.3% as chip stocks remained soft after Tuesday's rout despite a sharp Treasury-driven drop in long-term yields; no fresh TSM-specific catalyst was confirmed.

ASML.text: ASML fell 2.8% with the broader semiconductor complex as investors continued trimming AI and chip exposure despite Treasury-driven relief in long-term yields; no fresh ASML-specific catalyst was confirmed.

KLAC.text: KLA fell 3.9%, underperforming a modestly higher broad market as semiconductor shares remained under pressure in continued AI-chip de-risking; no fresh KLA-specific catalyst was confirmed.

INTC.text: Intel fell 4.0% with continued semiconductor weakness; no fresh Intel-specific catalyst was confirmed, while the recently completed $20 billion share sale remained a dilution and capital-raise overhang.

MU.text: Micron slipped 0.4% as memory and other AI-linked chip stocks remained volatile after Tuesday's sharp selloff; no fresh Micron-specific catalyst was confirmed.

DDOG.text: Datadog fell 5.1% despite a modestly higher Nasdaq; no fresh company-specific catalyst was confirmed, leaving the move consistent with continued volatility after its Aug. 6 reset around slower growth and reduced usage by its largest AI customer.

META.text: Meta edged up 0.4% as lower long-term Treasury yields supported the broader market, outweighing continued legal pressure from testimony in the 29-state youth-safety trial.

PLTR.text: Palantir rose 2.1% as falling long-term Treasury yields helped growth stocks recover; no fresh Palantir-specific catalyst was confirmed.

SPCX.text: SpaceX fell 2.6% ahead of Thursday's lockup expiration, when up to 319 million employee and early-investor shares become eligible for trading, adding potential supply to the market.
